title: The Superior Mechanical Resistance of Nexa® Vials for Improved Efficiency and Safety
summary: Breakage reduction starts with container strength. This article looks at mechanical resistance in pharma vials, with a focus on Stevanato Group’s Nexa®.
body_text: JAN 8 | 2025 The Superior Mechanical Resistance of Nexa® Vials for Improved Efficiency and Safety Executive Summary Introduction: Ensuring the mechanical resistance of pharmaceutical glass vials is crucial for safe and efficient drug delivery. While allowing for high throughput and efficiency, the bulk Fill & Finish process exerts high level of stress on glass containers, such as glass-to-glass contact and vertical loads, which can lead to cosmetic defects and breakages. Superior vial quality mitigates the negative impact of this stress, improving filling process performance and output as well as reducing the risk of container breakage during transport. 2R vials This study aims to experimentally demonstrate the improved mechanical resistance performance of Nexa®. By comparing the 2R ISO format vial in Nexa® and Fina® platforms, this study highlights how Nexa® vials provide superior mechanical resistance, which translates into several operational benefits. Test Methodology Mechanical resistance was assessed using two quantitative techniques 1. Vertical Compression Test (VC): This test measures the maximum force a vial can withstand before failure when subjected to axial stress. vertical compression_2R_pre and post Figure 1: Sample before (left) and after (right) VC test. 2. Burst Test (BT): This test is performed to apply internal pressure to the glass container to obtain its maximum value of internal pressure resistance. burst test_2R_pre and post Figure 2: Sample before (left) and after (right) the burst test. Both tests compared Nexa® and Fina® vials. From the results achieved (VC and BT), Nexa® vials showed consistent superior mechanical resistance . Key Results 2R ISO vials In the Vertical Compression Test , Nexa® vials demonstrated an average maximum force of at least 3x Fina®. vertical compression_2R Figure 3: Boxplot of Vertical Compression results for 2R Fina® and Nexa® vials. In the Burst Test , Nexa® vials are characterized by a higher mean value, in terms of maximum pressure, than Fina® vials. burst test_2R Figure 4: Boxplot of Burst Test Results for 2R Fina® and Nexa® vials Operational Benefits of Nexa® Vials - Thanks to their improved cosmetic quality and mechanical resistance, Nexa® vials provide several advantages: 01 Reduced Total Cost of Ownership (TCO): Fewer cosmetic rejections and in-line breakages reduce waste of both container and final product, which in turn lowers costs and prevents lost revenues. 02 Improved Efficiency: Nexa® vials result in fewer lines-stops, downtimes, and labor required to fix the filling line after breakage occurrence. 03 Higher Safety: The superior mechanical strength of Nexa® vials reduces the risk of harmful products being dispersed due to container breakage. Conclusions This study analyzed the improved mechanical resistance of Nexa® vials by comparing them to Fina® vials through vertical compression (VC) and burst test (BT). According to the results achieved, Nexa® vials have superior mechanical resistance, even 3x Fina® with regards to Vertical compression (VC). Thanks to its improved mechanical resistance, the Nexa® vial platform offers advantages in terms of: 01 Lower risk of breakage and cosmetic rejections reducing non-quality costs, and maximizing redictivity of high-value drug products 02 Lower risk of breakage to preserve people’s safety when dealing with cytotoxic products and to guarantee container integrity during challenging freezing processes. 2R vials with add ons Nexa® vial platform is Stevanato Group next level of quality specifically designed for most of high value products such as biotech , high-value vaccines , cytotoxic and next generation drugs . Thanks to their improved mechanical resistance and cosmetic quality Nexa® vials minimize product waste and product release into the environment during fill & finish process and final visual inspection. Additionally, Nexa® vials ensure lower vial breakage risk at challenging temperatures during freezing and cryo treatments . body_text: For advertisers, no quarter carries more weight than Q4, and 2026 is shaping up to be another strong one. EMARKETER predicts holiday spending will increase year-over-year (YoY), for retail as a whole and even more so for ecommerce. Q4 has always been competitive, but the holiday shopping landscape continues to shift in ways that make standing out harder than ever. Here’s what market research and MNTN advertiser data reveal about the trends shaping Q4 2026, and what they mean for your strategy. Streaming Owns the Largest Share of TV Viewership and Q4 Is When It Matters Most Streaming has cemented itself as the dominant way Americans watch television. As of April 2026 , it commanded 47.6% of U.S. household TV viewing (more than broadcast and cable combined). That split holds in Q4 too, and it may matter more during the holiday season than any other time of year. In December 2025 , streaming captured 47.5% of all TV viewing, while broadcast fell to 21.4% and cable dropped to 20.2%. And within the Q4 window, specific dates carry outsized weight. In 2025, streaming viewership was up 11% during Thanksgiving week and 19% during Christmas week, compared with average non-holiday weeks. As Q4 streaming viewership hits new highs, MNTN advertiser performance data points in the same direction. Among MNTN advertisers who ran campaigns in both Q4 2024 and Q4 2025, key metrics improved YoY, some by significant margins: +448% Average Conversion Rate +121% Average Average Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) +80% Average Visit Rate -10% Average Average Cost per Acquisition (CPA) Mobile shopping’s rise isn’t just about convenience: ever-growing second-screen usage is fueling it too. Nearly two-thirds of U.S. social network users are projected to be actively using a second screen while watching TV or streaming in 2026, a figure expected to reach 81.9% of the total U.S. population by 2027. And the shopping behavior that follows is measurable: 34% of U.S. TV viewers have purchased merchandise inspired by a show, and 31% have shopped for products tied to what they’re watching via QR codes or in-show links. Second-screen usage is surging across all age groups, and this is particularly notable in Q4. In November 2025, 63% of consumers ages 18-24 and 61% of those ages 25-34 viewed videos on their phones while watching TV (up 2% and 1% since 2022, respectively). But the most notable growth came from older generations: 52% of consumers ages 45-54 and 35% ages 55-64 also use a second screen while streaming, an increase of 13% and 15% since 2022. Travel Tuesday is Now One of Q4’s Most Valuable Moments for Travel Brands Q4 marks the unofficial start of Wave Season , the travel industry’s peak booking period, when consumers are actively planning trips months in advance. BFCM has long been a strong window for travel brands, but in recent years a new moment has emerged in its wake: Travel Tuesday (the day after Cyber Monday). Travel Tuesday now generates 3.5x more bookings than the average day, with searches for the event up more than 5x over a two-year period. Together, Black Friday, Cyber Monday, and Travel Tuesday have become what travel marketing agency Sojern refers to as a “perfect storm”: a concentrated window of urgency and deal volume covering flights, hotels, and packages. A “value-first traveler” mindset is reshaping how consumers engage with this shopping period. They’re still spending on travel, but choosing with precision, seeking packages, points, and experiences over premium-priced impulse bookings. MNTN advertiser data supports the importance of Q4 and Travel Tuesday in particular. Among travel brands active in both Q4 2024 and Q4 2025, the following key metrics improved YoY: +133% Average Visit Rate +56% Average ROAS +49% Average Conversion Rate On top of this, average CPA and CPV fell sharply. Within Q4, the week of Cyber Monday and Travel Tuesday was the strongest of the quarter across revenue, ROAS, and CPA. Travel Tuesday itself was the standout day of the entire BFCM window, driving the highest revenue, the lowest CPA, and an average order value (AOV) that was 147% higher than Black Friday. The implications of these findings extend beyond travel brands. Elevated purchase intent that builds through BFCM doesn’t switch off after Cyber Monday. Instead, it carries into the days that follow, and beyond. For advertisers in industries that can have longer purchase cycles (e.g. financial services, automotive, education, health, technology) the BFCM window is an opportunity to reach consumers who are already primed. Just as travel brands use Travel Tuesday to lock in bookings for trips months away, brands in other industries can use Q4 to plant intent that converts well into the new year. Video Game Spending Is Approaching All-Time Highs, and Q4 Is Make-or-Break U.S. consumer spending on video games reached $60.7 billion in 2025 (the second-highest on record) and 2026 has the potential to reach a new all-time high. Q4 is a key piece to this, as 45% of single-player games drop between mid-August and mid-November. This year, that includes the highly anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto VI on November 19th, which is expected to drive a significant spike in sales. The biggest structural shift in gaming right now is where spending happens. Physical game sales hit a 30-year low of $1.5 billion in 2025, even as total spending grew, driven by digital downloads, cloud gaming, and subscriptions. Subscription spending increased by 20% in 2025 , making it the single largest growth driver in the industry. This shift has real implications for how gaming audiences are reached: as consumers move away from physical retail and toward digital-based access (which will only accelerate in light of Sony’s decision to end physical disc production by early 2028) TV video content has become one of the most effective ways to connect with them. Gaming audiences aren’t just playing, they’re watching movies, sports, and shows like everyone else, making Q4’s record streaming environment a prime opportunity for gaming advertisers. For non-gaming brands, the subscription trend is a signal worth watching. Consumers are increasingly comfortable giving and receiving digital products as opposed to physical ones. For brands outside of gaming, Q4 is a prime window to position subscription offerings as gifts or purposeful new-year investments. ‘Tis the Season to Get Your Q4 Strategy Set Q4 2026 is set up to be one of the most opportunity-rich on record. Streaming reach is at an all-time high, and mobile has permanently shifted how consumers shop during the holidays. Meanwhile, moments like Travel Tuesday and major gaming releases are concentrating purchase intent in specific windows that produce powerful performance. Brands that understand where that intent lives (and show up there consistently) will be the ones that make the most of it. For advertisers looking to reach engaged, high-intent holiday audiences across all of these moments, Connected TV (CTV) is uniquely positioned to deliver.

title: AI Is Exposing Fragmented Systems in Financial Services
summary: AI exposes fragmented systems in financial services. Integrated data, simplified operations, and real-time intelligence are critical.
body_text: The biggest problem in financial services is not AI readiness, it’s structural complexity. Video: How SAP and SAP Fioneer Are Shaping the Future Watch now That was the takeaway from a recent conversation between SAP CFO Dominik Asam and SAP Fioneer CEO Matthias Tomann. Their conversation touched on topics like the future of financial services , the role of AI, and the growing importance of integrated enterprise platforms. For decades, banks and insurers have built operating models around regulatory fragmentation, country-specific requirements, layered systems, and continuous workaround solutions. As a result, the industry is running on patchwork architecture that is expensive to maintain, slow to change, and fundamentally misaligned with how AI works. Partnership built for financial services innovation Since joining forces in 2021, SAP and SAP Fioneer have significantly expanded their joint capabilities for the financial services sector. As Tomann highlighted in the conversation, the partnership has already delivered substantial momentum for SAP Fioneer: R&D investment increased by 120% Annual software sales more than doubled Major customers successfully transitioned to SAP Cloud ERP The platform evolved into a richer, more scalable, and highly capable ecosystem Together, the companies are combining SAP’s trusted cloud and data infrastructure with SAP Fioneer’s deep financial services expertise to help institutions simplify operations, modernize core systems, and prepare for the AI-driven future. Executives from both companies will be exploring these critical topics further at their annual SAP & SAP Fioneer Financial Services Forum 2026, which is now open for registration. AI is not the starting point, data integration is Everyone wants AI, but AI can only create value from integrated data, real-time access, and standardized processes. But most financial institutions still operate on the opposite: fragmented foundations. That reality will define the winners over the next five years. The organizations that succeed will not be the ones experimenting with the most models. They will be the ones that establish unified, trusted, real-time enterprise data with strong governance. That is the real competitive advantage. But even that is only part of the story. The next phase is not just about using AI to analyze better; it is about AI executing work. We are now seeing a fundamental shift: from systems that store and report information to systems that act on that information in real time, orchestrating end-to-end processes across the business. This marks the transition to the Autonomous Enterprise , SAP’s vision for the future of business where AI does not just support decisions but increasingly drives execution, within clearly defined guardrails. Financial services can no longer afford “patchwork architecture” This shift makes one thing clear: The traditional approach to building IT landscapes is no longer viable. For years, many financial institutions solved problems incrementally—another point solution, another integration layer, another workaround. But eventually every workaround becomes technical debt and integration is the single largest IT cost category. Tomann made clear during the conversation that the emphasis must be on simplification rather than adding more complexity. What SAP and SAP Fioneer are driving is not another modernization cycle. It is a structural shift toward comprehensive, integrated platforms and AI driven processes that replace fragmentation, not sit on top of it. The result is a scalable financial services platform where core banking, lending, reporting, insurance, and analytics operate within an integrated architecture instead of disconnected silos. Real-time finance is becoming a strategic requirement Real-time capability is becoming foundational to competitiveness—whether it’s risk management, regulatory reporting, customer experience, fraud prevention, treasury operations, or AI-driven decision making. Institutions that can act on integrated data instantly will have a major advantage over those still moving information between disconnected systems overnight. With integrated data and AI embedded in core processes, finance is moving toward continuous financial intelligence: Forecasting becomes dynamic and always up to date Risk is detected and assessed in real time Closing processes become increasingly automated Decisions are guided by AI based on live business context Increasingly, AI assistants and agents take over execution of finance processes, from planning and risk management to invoicing and financial close, under strict governance. The role of finance shifts from reporting on the business to steering the business in real time. AI will reward those who simplify One of the most striking statements from Asam during the discussion is that SAP is already seeing 10x performance improvements from AI-driven process improvements. But it also highlights something many organizations still underestimate: just how much AI rewards those who standardize. The more fragmented the processes and data structures are, the harder it becomes to operationalize AI at scale. In contrast, organizations with standardized platforms, harmonized data, and integrated workflows will accelerate much faster. That is why modernization conversations today are no longer simply “IT projects.” They are business strategy discussions. Future of financial services will be built on trust, scale, and intelligence Financial services organizations are operating in an increasingly complex geopolitical and regulatory environment. Infrastructure decisions are no longer just about performance and cost, they are about compliance, security, operational resilience, and national requirements. This is why scalable, enterprise-grade cloud platforms are becoming so critical. The institutions that thrive in the next era of financial services will be the ones that can combine trusted data, integrated operations, AI-enabled processes, scalable infrastructure, and regulatory resilience into a single operating model. The future of financial services will not be defined by isolated AI experiments. It will be defined by who can build the most intelligent, connected, and adaptable enterprise foundation for what comes next. Learn more about SAP solutions for financial services here . Its platform-agnostic autonomy stack combines real-time sensor fusion, adaptive AI models, and edge-native orchestration, without vendor lock-in, to support autonomous and collaborative systems across air, ground, maritime, and industrial domains where performance, resilience, and trust are paramount. Notice Period Rules in India: Duration, Buy-Out, Recovery & Legal Rights 2026
summary: A comprehensive guide covering notice period laws, industry-wise duration, buyout calculation, garden leave, recovery rules, relieving letters, and employee & employer rights under Indian labour laws.
body_text: Insights & Resources Notice Period Rules in India: Duration, Buy-Out, Recovery & Legal Rights 2026 July 23, 2026 Shashank Yadav No comments yet 1. What is a Notice Period? A notice period is the duration of time between an employee’s resignation (or termination by the employer) and their last working day in the organisation. It serves as a critical transition window that allows both parties to prepare for the separation in an orderly manner. During this period, the outgoing employee is expected to: • Complete pending tasks and ongoing projects • Hand over responsibilities, documents, and knowledge to a successor or team • Return company assets such as laptops, ID cards, access badges, and keys • Facilitate knowledge transfer sessions for continuity • Allow the employer adequate time to recruit or reassign a replacement For the employer, the notice period provides a buffer against sudden departures that could disrupt operations, damage client relationships, or cause loss of institutional knowledge. For the employee, it offers time to wrap up professional relationships and ensure a clean exit that protects their professional reputation and future career prospects. Key Point In India, notice periods are primarily governed by employment contracts and offer letters, not a single central law. The actual duration depends on your contract, company policy, seniority level, and the applicable state-level Shops & Establishments Act. 2. Legal Framework: Laws Governing Notice Period in India Unlike many Western countries where notice periods are standardised by national labour law, India does not have a single central statute that mandates a specific notice period for all private-sector employees. Instead, the legal framework is a patchwork of central laws, state regulations, and contractual provisions. 2.1 Industrial Relations Code, 2020 The Industrial Relations Code (IRC) 2020, which subsumes the Industrial Disputes Act 1947, applies primarily to “workers” and “workmen” in industrial establishments. Key provisions include: • Retrenchment Notice: Employers must give 1 month’s written notice (or pay in lieu) when retrenching workers in establishments with fewer than 300 employees. • For establishments with 100-299 workers: The notice period for retrenchment has been effectively increased to 60 days under the new provisions. • Establishments with 300+ workers: Prior government approval is mandatory before retrenchment, layoff, or closure. A simple notice is not sufficient. • Worker resignation: A worker must give 14 days’ notice before going on strike; for resignation, the contract or standing orders govern. 2.2 State Shops & Establishments Acts Each Indian state has its own Shops & Establishments Act that governs working conditions for commercial establishments, shops, restaurants, theatres, and other non-factory entities. Notice period provisions vary by state: • Maharashtra: 30 days’ notice or salary in lieu for termination after 3 months of service. • Karnataka: 30 days’ notice or pay in lieu for employees with more than 6 months of service. • Delhi: 30 days’ notice or salary in lieu for employees with more than 3 months of service. • Tamil Nadu: 30 days’ notice for termination of employees who have completed 6 months. • Gujarat: 30 days’ notice or salary in lieu for permanent employees. 2.3 Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (OSH) Code, 2020 The OSH Code applies to establishments with 10 or more workers and contract labour. While it primarily addresses workplace safety, it also contains provisions related to employment terms and conditions, including notice requirements for certain categories of workers. 2.4 Employment Contracts & Offer Letters For the vast majority of private-sector employees, especially in IT, BFSI, consulting, and other white-collar industries, the notice period is determined entirely by the employment contract or offer letter. These contractual notice periods are legally binding, provided they are reasonable and not unconscionable. Important Courts have generally upheld contractual notice periods of up to 90 days as reasonable. However, excessively long notice periods (such as 6 months) or unreasonable penalty clauses may be struck down as restraint of trade under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872. 3. Notice Period Duration by Industry Notice period durations in India vary significantly across industries and seniority levels. The following table provides a comprehensive overview of standard notice periods across major sectors: Industry Junior / Entry Level Mid Level Senior / Leadership IT / Software 30 days 60 days 90 days BFSI (Banking, Finance) 30 days 60 days 90 days Manufacturing 30 days 30-60 days 60-90 days Startups 15-30 days 30 days 30-60 days Retail / Hospitality 15 days 30 days 30-60 days Pharma / Healthcare 30 days 60 days 90 days FMCG 30 days 30-60 days 60-90 days BPO / KPO 15-30 days 30 days 60 days Government / PSU 1-3 months 3 months 3 months India’s IT sector has among the highest notice periods globally . Major IT services companies such as TCS, Infosys, Wipro, and HCL Technologies typically require 90 days (3 months) of notice for confirmed employees. This is significantly longer than the 2-4 week standard in the United States or the 1-month standard in most European countries. The rationale for extended notice periods in IT includes the time needed for client relationship transition, project handover, knowledge documentation, and the critical nature of ongoing technology projects. Industry Insight Startups typically have the shortest notice periods (15-30 days) as they prioritise agility and speed. In contrast, Government and PSU roles often involve the longest notice periods (up to 3 months), reflecting bureaucratic processes and the time needed for formal transfers and charge handover. 4. Notice Period During Probation Probation periods are trial phases during which both the employer and the employee assess mutual fit. Notice period rules during probation are notably different from those applicable to confirmed employees. Standard Probation Notice Periods • Typical range: 7 to 30 days (as specified in the appointment letter) • Some companies allow termination with just 24 hours’ notice during probation • Probation notice is almost always shorter than the confirmed employee notice period • If not explicitly specified in the appointment letter, a reasonable notice of 15-30 days is generally expected by labour courts Key Considerations During probation, the employment relationship is more flexible. However, this does not mean either party can leave without any notice. Courts have held that even during probation, the principles of natural justice and fairness apply. • Always check your appointment letter for the specific probation notice clause • If the probation period is extended, the probation notice period typically continues to apply • Some companies require a different notice period once probation is confirmed mid-way • Exit during probation generally does not attract recovery or buyout penalties Pro Tip Before joining any organisation, carefully read the probation clause in your offer letter. Understand not just the duration of probation but also the notice period during probation, performance review criteria, and what happens if probation is extended. 5. Notice Period Buy-Out: Calculation & Process A notice period buy-out occurs when an employee (or their new employer) pays the current employer an amount equivalent to salary for the remaining unserved notice days, in order to leave before completing the full notice period. 5.1 When is Buy-Out Used? • Employee has received a better offer and the new employer needs them to join urgently • Personal or family reasons require an early departure • The employee is relocating to a different city or country • Critical project deadlines at the new employer require immediate joining • Mutual agreement between employee and current employer to end the relationship sooner 5.2 Buy-Out Calculation Formula Notice Period Buy-Out Formula Buy-Out Amount = (Monthly Salary / 30) x Unserved Notice Days Important: Some companies calculate the buy-out based on Basic Salary only, while others use Gross Salary (Basic + DA + HRA + other fixed components). Always refer to your employment contract for the exact clause. 5.3 Buy-Out Example Worked Example Employee: Rahul, Software Engineer at a Bengaluru IT firm Notice period: 90 days | Days served: 30 days | Unserved days: 60 days Monthly Gross Salary: Rs 80,000 Buy-Out = (Rs 80,000 / 30) x 60 = Rs 1,60,000 Rahul (or his new employer) must pay Rs 1,60,000 to the current employer for early release. 5.4 Who Pays the Buy-Out? Scenario Who Pays Notes Employee resigns & wants early release Employee Deducted from F&F or paid separately New employer reimburses New Employer Common in IT for senior hires Employer releases early (employer-initiated) Employer Must pay salary for full notice period Mutual agreement Negotiable Can agree on reduced amount or waiver 5.5 Tax Implications of Buy-Out • When employer pays notice salary in lieu of notice: Taxable as salary income for the employee under the Income Tax Act. • When employee pays buy-out to employer: This amount is NOT deductible as an expense under Income Tax for the employee. It is treated as a personal expense. • When new employer reimburses buy-out: The reimbursement is part of the new employment terms and is typically taxable as part of salary or a joining bonus. 6. Notice Period Recovery: What Employers Can Deduct When an employee leaves without serving the full notice period (and without a buy-out arrangement), the employer has the right to recover the notice period shortfall. This is known as notice period recovery. 6.1 Recovery Mechanism Employers have several mechanisms for recovering notice period dues: 1. Deduction from Full & Final (F&F) Settlement: The most common method. The employer deducts the unserved notice pay from the employee’s F&F amount, which includes pending salary, earned leave encashment, bonus, and other dues. 2. Withholding Relieving Letter: The employer can withhold the relieving letter and experience certificate until all dues (including notice recovery) are cleared. This is a powerful leverage point. 3. Civil Recovery: If the F&F settlement is insufficient to cover the recovery amount, the employer can pursue civil remedies under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 by filing a civil suit for breach of contract. 4. Background Verification Flag: Absence of a relieving letter is flagged by background verification agencies, which can impact the employee’s future job prospects. 6.2 Recovery Calculation Notice Period Recovery Formula Recovery = (Basic or Gross Salary as per contract / 30) x Unserved Days The exact salary component used for calculation (Basic Salary vs. Gross Salary) depends on the specific clause in your employment contract. In the absence of a specific clause, courts generally consider Basic Salary as the basis for recovery. Warning Absconding from a job without serving any notice period can have serious consequences. Beyond financial recovery, it can result in being blacklisted by the company (and sometimes the entire group), negative references during background checks, and difficulty obtaining a relieving letter. Always try to negotiate an early release rather than absconding. 7. Garden Leave: Meaning, Rules & Comparison Garden leave (also called “gardening leave”) is a period during which an employee who has resigned or been terminated remains on the company’s payroll but is not required to attend office or perform any work. The term originates from the British practice of “sending the employee home to tend their garden.” 7.1 Key Features of Garden Leave • The employee receives full salary and benefits during the garden leave period • The employee cannot join another employer or engage in competing business activities • Access to company systems, email, client lists, and confidential data is revoked • Commonly used for senior employees in competitive industries such as IT, BFSI, and management consulting • Duration is typically the full notice period or a significant part of it • The arrangement is legally enforceable as part of the employment contract 7.2 When Do Companies Use Garden Leave? • When a senior employee is joining a direct competitor • When the employee has access to highly sensitive client data or trade secrets • When there is a risk of the employee poaching colleagues or clients • When the company wants to ensure confidential strategic plans remain protected • When knowledge transfer is already complete, and physical presence adds no value 7.3 Garden Leave vs Notice Period vs Paid Leave Feature Notice Period (Working) Garden Leave Paid Leave Works for company? Yes No No Receives salary? Yes Yes Yes Can join competitor? No No (explicitly barred) N/A Company system access? Yes (full) No (revoked) No Knowledge transfer? Yes (primary purpose) No (already completed) N/A Purpose Smooth transition Competitive protection Rest & personal time Common for All employees Senior roles All employees Legal Note Garden leave clauses are generally enforceable in India because, unlike non-compete clauses (which are void under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 post-employment), garden leave restricts activity during the employment period when the contract is still active and the employee is being compensated. 8. Early Release & Notice Period Waiver There are several scenarios where the full notice period may be shortened or waived entirely. Understanding these can help employees plan their transitions more effectively. Scenarios for Shortened Notice 1. Mutual Agreement: Both the employee and employer agree to a shorter notice period. This is the most common and smoothest route to early release. 2. Employee Buy-Out: The employee pays for the remaining unserved notice days. The employer is not obligated to accept a buy-out, but most companies have a buy-out provision in their policy. 3. Employer-Initiated Early Release: The employer decides to release the employee early. In this case, the employer must pay salary for the full contractual notice period. 4. Medical Emergency: Employees facing genuine medical emergencies (with supporting documentation from a registered medical practitioner) are often granted early release on humanitarian grounds. 5. No Critical Handover Needed: If the employee’s role does not involve critical projects or client relationships, and a replacement is already available, the employer may waive the remaining notice. 6. Replacement Already Hired: If the company has already found and onboarded a replacement, the remaining notice period may serve no practical purpose and can be waived. Negotiation Tip When requesting early release, frame it as a win-win. Offer to complete all handover documentation, train your replacement, and be available for questions via email or phone after your last day. Managers are more likely to grant early release when they feel confident that the transition will be smooth. 9. Legal Rights of Employees During Notice Period Employees in India have several important legal rights during their notice period. Understanding these rights ensures you are treated fairly and can make informed decisions. 1. Right to Resign: Every employee has the fundamental right to resign from employment. An employer cannot prevent an employee from resigning. The resignation takes effect once the notice period is served or bought out. 2. Right to Receive Full Salary: During the notice period, the employee is entitled to their full salary, allowances, and benefits as per their employment terms. The employer cannot reduce salary during notice. 3. Right to Use Earned Leave: Employees can utilise their accrued earned leave during the notice period, subject to company policy. Accrued earned leave is a statutory entitlement that cannot be forfeited. 4. Right to Receive a Relieving Letter: After serving the complete notice period and clearing all dues, the employee has the right to receive a relieving letter. Unreasonable withholding can be challenged in a Labour Court. 5. Right to Full & Final Settlement: The employee is entitled to receive their F&F settlement, including pending salary, leave encashment, bonus, and gratuity (if applicable), within 2 working days of their last working day under the new Labour Codes. 6. Right to Negotiate: Employees have the right to negotiate the notice period duration, request early release, or discuss buy-out terms. The employer is not obligated to agree, but negotiation is a legitimate right. 7. Right to Challenge Unfair Clauses: If the notice period clause in the employment contract is unconscionable or amounts to a restraint of trade, the employee can challenge it before a civil court or Labour Court. 10. Legal Rights of Employers Employers also have significant legal rights when it comes to notice periods. Understanding these rights helps employers protect their interests while ensuring compliance with labour laws. 1. Right to Enforce Contractual Notice: Employers can enforce the notice period as agreed in the employment contract. If the employee fails to serve notice, the employer can initiate recovery proceedings. 2. Right to Recover Notice Pay: If the employee leaves without serving the full notice, the employer can deduct the equivalent salary from the F&F settlement or pursue civil recovery. 3. Right to Withhold Relieving Letter: The employer can withhold the relieving letter and experience certificate until all outstanding dues, including notice period recovery, are cleared by the employee. 4. Right to Impose Garden Leave: Employers can place employees on garden leave during the notice period, restricting access to systems and clients while continuing to pay salary. 5. Right to Enforce Non-Compete During Notice: While post-employment non-compete clauses are generally void under Indian law, employers can enforce non-compete restrictions during the active notice period. 6. Right to Civil Remedies: For material breach of the employment contract (such as absconding or joining a competitor during notice), the employer can pursue civil remedies including injunctive relief and damages. 7. Right to Conduct Exit Process: Employers have the right to mandate exit interviews, asset return, knowledge transfer documentation, and security clearance as part of the notice period process. 11. Notice Period & Leaves: Can You Take Leave? One of the most frequently asked questions by employees serving notice is whether they can take leave during the notice period. The answer depends on company policy, the type of leave, and the terms of the employment contract. Types of Leave During Notice Leave Type Generally Allowed? Impact on Notice Period Earned Leave / Privilege Leave Yes (or encashed) Does not extend notice (most companies) Casual Leave Restricted by most companies May extend notice by equivalent days Sick Leave (with medical cert.) Yes (genuine illness) May extend notice by equivalent days Maternity / Paternity Leave Yes (statutory right) Runs concurrently or post-notice Compensatory Off At employer discretion Does not extend notice Leave Without Pay (LWP) Rare during notice Extends notice by equivalent days Key Rules • Most companies restrict casual leave and discourage sick leave during the notice period unless supported by a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner. • Accrued earned leave is a statutory right. The employer cannot force forfeiture of earned leave; it can either be utilised (if the company allows) or encashed as part of the F&F settlement. • Some company policies state that any leave taken during notice extends the notice period by an equivalent number of days. Check your employee handbook or HR policy document for this clause. • Public holidays and weekly offs do NOT extend the notice period as they are not classified as leave. Best Practice If you plan to take leave during your notice period, communicate early with your manager and HR. Getting approval in writing (email confirmation) protects you from disputes about your last working day and F&F settlement date. 12. Relieving Letter: Importance & Rules The relieving letter is arguably the most important document issued at the end of an employment relationship. It serves as formal confirmation that the employee has been officially released from all duties and obligations. 12.1 What a Relieving Letter Contains • Full name of the employee • Employee ID or reference number • Designation and department at the time of exit • Date of joining and last working day • Confirmation that all company assets have been returned • Confirmation that all dues have been settled • Statement that the employee has been officially relieved from duties 12.2 Why is the Relieving Letter Critical? • Background Verification: Most reputable employers conduct background verification for new hires. The absence of a relieving letter from a previous employer is a major red flag that can lead to offer withdrawal. • Future Employment: Many employers require the relieving letter as a mandatory joining document. Without it, the new employer may not process your onboarding. • Legal Proof: The relieving letter serves as legal proof that you left your previous employment on good terms and fulfilled all contractual obligations. • Professional Reputation: A clean exit with a proper relieving letter reflects professionalism and protects your long-term career reputation. 12.3 What if the Employer Withholds the Relieving Letter? An employer cannot unreasonably withhold the relieving letter once the employee has served the notice period and cleared all dues. If the employer withholds without valid reason: • Step 1: Send a formal written request (email with acknowledgement) to HR and your reporting manager. • Step 2: Escalate to senior management with documented proof of notice served and dues cleared. • Step 3: Approach the Labour Commissioner or file a complaint with the local Labour Court. • Step 4: Courts can direct the employer to issue the relieving letter and may award compensation for the delay. 13. New Labour Codes 2026: What Changed The new Labour Codes, which consolidate 29 existing labour laws into 4 comprehensive codes, have introduced several changes that impact notice period rules and exit management in India. Key Changes Affecting Notice Periods Provision Old Rule New Rule (2026) Retrenchment Notice (100-299 workers) 30 days 60 days Establishments with 300+ workers Govt. permission for 100+ (some states) Govt. permission mandatory for 300+ (nationwide) F&F Settlement Timeline No statutory deadline Within 2 working days of last working day Fixed-Term Contracts Not clearly defined End of contract = end of obligation; no separate notice Standing Orders Applicable to 100+ workers Threshold may be revised based on state notification Impact on Employees • Faster F&F Settlements: The 2-working-day mandate for F&F settlement ensures employees receive their dues promptly upon exit. Previously, F&F could be delayed for weeks or even months. • Fixed-Term Clarity: Employees on fixed-term contracts now have clarity that the contract end date is the natural conclusion of the employment, and no separate notice period applies. • Greater Protection for Workers: The increased retrenchment notice period (60 days for establishments with 100-299 workers) provides a longer buffer for affected workers to find alternative employment. Impact on Employers • Compliance Burden: The 2-day F&F settlement timeline requires employers to have robust exit management and payroll systems in place. • Higher Retrenchment Threshold: The requirement of government approval for retrenchment in establishments with 300+ workers adds a procedural step that can delay workforce restructuring. • Documentation Requirements: Employers must maintain detailed records of notice periods served, buy-out payments, and F&F settlements to demonstrate compliance during audits. 14. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) Q: What is a notice period? A: A notice period is the duration between an employee’s resignation or termination and their last working day. It allows time for knowledge transfer, project handover, and replacement hiring. The duration is typically specified in the employment contract or offer letter. Q: What is the typical notice period in IT companies in India? A: Most large IT companies in India (TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCL) require 90 days (3 months) of notice for confirmed employees. Junior or entry-level employees may have 30-day notice periods, while mid-level roles typically require 60 days. Q: Can I resign without serving the notice period? A: Yes, you can resign at any time as resignation is a fundamental right. However, if you do not serve the notice period, the employer can deduct notice pay from your Full & Final settlement, withhold your relieving letter, and in extreme cases, pursue civil recovery under the Indian Contract Act, 1872. Q: What is notice period buy-out? A: A buy-out is when the employee (or their new employer) pays the current employer salary for the unserved notice days in order to leave early. The formula is: (Monthly Salary / 30) x Unserved Notice Days. The exact salary component (Basic or Gross) depends on the employment contract. Q: How is notice period recovery calculated? A: Recovery = (Basic Salary or Gross Salary as per contract / 30) x Number of Unserved Days. The employer deducts this from the F&F settlement. If the F&F amount is insufficient, the employer can pursue civil recovery. Q: What is garden leave? A: Garden leave is a period where the employee remains on the company payroll but does not work or attend office. The employee receives full salary but cannot join a competitor or access company systems. It is commonly used for senior employees in competitive industries to protect sensitive business information. Q: Can an employer force a 90-day notice period? A: Yes, if the 90-day notice period is specified in your signed employment contract or offer letter, it is legally enforceable. Courts have upheld notice periods of up to 90 days as reasonable. However, notice periods longer than 90 days may be challenged if deemed unreasonable. Q: Is a notice period mandatory during probation? A: Probation notice periods are typically shorter (7-30 days) and may even allow termination with 24 hours’ notice. The specific terms are defined in your appointment letter. If no notice period is mentioned for probation, a reasonable notice of 15-30 days is generally expected. Q: Can I take leave during the notice period? A: This depends on your company’s leave policy. Most companies restrict casual leave during notice but allow utilisation or encashment of earned leave. Sick leave with a valid medical certificate is usually permitted. Some companies extend the notice period by the number of leave days taken. Q: What if my employer does not give me a relieving letter? A: If you have served your complete notice period and cleared all dues, the employer cannot unreasonably withhold the relieving letter. You can send a formal written request, escalate to senior management, and if necessary, approach the Labour Commissioner or Labour Court for relief. Q: What are the notice period rules under the new Labour Codes? A: The new Labour Codes increased the retrenchment notice from 30 to 60 days for establishments with 100-299 workers, mandate F&F settlement within 2 working days, and clarify that fixed-term contracts end naturally without requiring separate notice. Government approval is needed for retrenchment in establishments with 300+ workers. Q: Can the notice period be negotiated? A: Yes, notice periods can be negotiated between the employee and employer. This can happen at the time of joining (negotiating a shorter notice clause in the offer letter) or at the time of resignation (requesting early release). However, the employer is not obligated to agree to a shorter notice period. Related Shashank Yadav Leave a Reply Cancel reply

title: Sales Pipeline Management: A Step-by-Step Guide for Sales Leaders
summary: Learn how to manage your sales pipeline effectively with this step-by-step guide for sales leaders to improve forecasting, conversions, and revenue.
body_text: Companies that become skilled at specific sales pipeline management practices achieve 28% higher revenue growth than their competitors. Sales teams generate 18% more revenue with well-laid-out processes compared to those without structured approaches. The surprising fact remains that very few organizations make these practices work. Sales professionals spend only 20% of their time facing customers . The other 80% goes into background tasks, particularly in AI and SaaS industries. This background work determines success through effective pipeline management. This piece will guide you through a practical approach to sales pipeline management that can improve your sales outcomes. You'll learn everything from core components to implementing best practices. We'll show you the exact steps to build and manage a results-driven sales pipeline. Let's tuck into the details! What is a sales pipeline? A sales pipeline shows where your potential customers stand in your sales process . Your team tracks each step to turn leads into paying customers while gathering information about possible deals and what they might be worth. Sales funnels look at things from the customer's side, but a pipeline reveals your internal sales process—how your team works through specific stages to close deals. This well-laid-out approach helps sales teams focus on opportunities that will likely bring the highest returns. Companies with optimized sales pipelines grow their revenue 28% faster according to research [link_2]. Teams that follow formal pipeline processes saw their pipeline grow 28% year-over-year, while companies without effective management faced a 7% decline. A well-built pipeline offers several key benefits: You see upcoming sales opportunities clearly Your revenue forecasts become more accurate You spot process bottlenecks quickly Your prospects receive systematic nurturing Your resources get allocated better Why pipeline visibility matters? Pipeline visibility gives sales teams a clear picture of their process and pipeline health . Teams can make evidence-based decisions using live information that leads to better forecasting, smarter resource use, and stronger team accountability. On top of that, it helps identify promising leads , stops small problems from growing, and makes sure everyone knows their targets and how they're doing. What is Sales Pipeline Management? Sales pipeline management tracks and guides potential customers through different stages of the buying trip. The process actively oversees prospects from their original contact to closed deals. This creates a reliable sales plan that prioritizes promising opportunities and predicts future business outcomes. The pipeline management process needs several activities to work . These include lead qualification, activity tracking, forecasting, regular pipeline reviews, and CRM integration. Together, these activities boost conversion rates, reduce sales cycles, enhance forecast accuracy, and maintain consistent prospect follow-ups. Common challenges in pipeline sales Many organizations face difficulties with pipeline management. Research shows 63% of sales managers believe their organization poorly manages its pipeline. Here are the most important challenges they face: Data quality issues : B2B data becomes outdated by 30% each year as people change jobs and companies relocate Inconsistent follow-ups : About 44% of sales reps quit after one follow-up, though most deals need five or more contacts Team misalignment : The disconnect between sales and marketing teams creates blame games and missed revenue opportunities Stalled deals : These happen because of delayed internal approvals, pricing objections, or competitor interference Lengthy sales cycles : About 27% of sales reps see long sales cycles as their main obstacle to reaching quota Sales leaders also struggle with oversized pipelines. These pipelines contain outdated opportunities that skew forecasts and waste valuable selling time. What are the core components of pipeline management? Sales pipeline management works best when several connected parts come together to track and close deals. Five essential elements are the foundations of pipeline management: tracking progress, forecasting , resource allocation, process optimization, and performance analysis. Each part plays a unique role to move prospects through your sales process quickly. You need the right tools to make your pipeline work. A good system has CRM software that centralizes customer data, sales analytics to measure key metrics, communication platforms for team collaboration, and sales enablement resources that help reps build their skills. Your metrics and analytics should collect and analyze pipeline data to learn about each stage . These numbers help spot bottlenecks, track conversion rates, and measure how fast deals move. A standardized sales process helps your team stay consistent. Your pipeline stages need clear definitions and specific criteria to move prospects forward. The pipeline needs regular cleaning to keep data accurate. Remove stale deals, update opportunity details, and make sure your pipeline shows the real picture instead of just hopeful thinking. These components create a clear view of your revenue pipeline. The analytical insights you gain help improve sales performance and business growth. 8 Best Practices for Managing a Sales Pipeline Sales teams that adopt proven pipeline management practices see better results. Research shows companies that become skilled at specific pipeline management practices achieve 28% faster revenue growth . 1. Monitor key sales metrics regularly You need to track vital pipeline metrics such as conversion rates between stages (target 20-30%) , average sales cycle length, win rate (15-20% industry average), and pipeline velocity . Your dashboards should show immediate performance data that helps spot bottlenecks quickly. 2. Standardize your sales process Companies with well-laid-out sales processes make 18% more revenue than their competitors. You should set clear definitions for each pipeline stage and specific criteria that move deals forward. This approach reduces inconsistencies and leads to predictable outcomes. 3. Keep opportunity data updated A clean pipeline needs regular reviews and updated contact details without duplicates . When you use automated activity capture, it removes manual data entry and ensures everyone has accurate information. 4. Qualify deals with a clear framework Your team should use structured qualification frameworks like BANT, MEDDIC, or CHAMP . A properly qualified opportunity meets five core criteria: budget reality, authority mapping, need validation, decision process, and competitive position. 5. Follow up consistently and strategically The data shows 80% of sales need at least five follow-ups , yet 44% of sales reps quit after one attempt. A response within an hour makes prospects seven times more likely to engage. 6. Focus on high-value opportunities The best performers choose accounts with highest growth potential instead of spreading resources thin. Lead scoring helps assess prospects based on ideal customer profile fit, budget availability, and engagement level. 7. Line up sales with marketing and customer success Teams that work well together see up to 72% higher profitability. Regular cross-departmental meetings ensure smooth handoffs and consistent customer experience throughout the buyer's journey. 8. Use CRM and automation tools effectively Your team should utilize CRM features to automate routine tasks , maintain consistent processes, and get valuable analytics. This automation cuts down manual data entry and saves up to 200 hours yearly per user for actual selling activities. What are the benefits of effective pipeline management? Proper sales pipeline management does more than just organize your work—it directly affects your bottom line. Companies that manage their pipelines well are 10% more likely to grow their revenue year after year. Some companies even see growth rates 15-28% higher than their competitors. Revenue and performance improvements happen in several ways. Sales teams can see their active deals better, which helps them focus on the most valuable opportunities. They can track both the number and quality of leads as they move through each sales stage. Data-driven decision making becomes easier because pipeline management shows clear metrics. Resource optimization happens naturally when managers utilize up-to-the-minute pipeline data to assign team tasks. Good pipeline management makes forecasting more accurate. Businesses can set revenue targets, predict future sales changes, and spot new areas for growth. Team development gets better because managers can see how individuals and teams perform. This visibility lets them coach team members who need help. Customer relationships grow stronger through regular follow-ups and after-sale involvement. This leads to better customer retention and more customized interactions based on what prospects need and want. Conclusion Sales pipeline management revolutionizes how sales teams operate and deliver results. This piece shows how structured approaches boost revenue substantially while poor processes waste opportunities. Sales leaders should prioritize proper pipeline management implementation. These eight best practices create a clear path to success. Each practice tackles specific challenges that often hurt sales efforts - from keeping track of metrics to following up strategically. These aren't just theories but proven strategies with solid performance data to back them up. Teams that stick to these principles see faster sales cycles , better conversion rates, and more precise forecasts. On top of that, it creates continuous connection between sales, marketing, and customer success teams that builds stronger bonds with customers. Your pipeline management needs both good tools and processes to work well . CRM systems help automate daily tasks, but they need to work with standard qualification frameworks and regular maintenance. This mix will give a clean database while your team focuses on valuable opportunities. Start by fixing one problem area instead of changing everything at once . Your team might not deal very well with regular follow-ups or need better stage definitions. Small changes often create big results when teams apply them consistently. Sales pipeline management puts teams in charge of their success rather than leaving it to chance. Teams can achieve steady revenue growth even in tough markets through better visibility, accountability, and structure. Qualified leads must be ideal customers with the right need and budget. They move through set stages that match clear steps in the buyer's trip. What is the cost of poor pipeline management?
